name: Glycolysis
description: Breakdown of glucose → 2 pyruvate. Net yield: 2 ATP (anaerobic) or 7 ATP (aerobic). Occurs in cytoplasm of all cells.

disorder.name: Tarui Disease (GSD VII)
branch: Cannot use glucose for ATP during exercise

disorder.name: Hereditary Fructose Intolerance
branch: Jaundice, vomiting, hepatomegaly after fruit intake

disorder.name: Inhibited by Iodoacetate / Arsenate
branch: Arsenate replaces Pᵢ → forms 1-arseno-3-phosphoglycerate → hydrolyses spontaneously
Uncouples substrate-level ATP production (1,3-BPG never forms)

steps.cofactors: H₂O removed; Mg²⁺ or Mn²⁺ required

disorder.name: Fluoride inhibits Enolase
branch: Stops glycolysis in RBCs in blood collection tubes
Used clinically to prevent ex-vivo glucose consumption

disorder.name: Pyruvate Kinase Deficiency
branch: ↓ ATP → RBC membrane failure and haemolysis

finalMolecule: Pyruvate (×2)

name: Gluconeogenesis
description: Synthesis of glucose from non-carbohydrate precursors (lactate, amino acids, glycerol, propionyl CoA). Occurs in liver and kidney cortex. Requires 6 high-energy phosphate bonds per glucose.

steps.cofactors: ATP + CO₂ + Biotin; activated by Acetyl-CoA

disorder.name: Pyruvate Carboxylase Deficiency
branch: Cannot replenish oxaloacetate for TCA or gluconeogenesis

steps.cofactors: OAA → Malate (cannot cross membrane as OAA)

steps.enzyme: Reversible Glycolytic Enzymes (Enolase, Mutase, PGK, GAPDH)

steps.cofactors: H₂O; inhibited by AMP and Fructose-2,6-BP

disorder.name: Fructose-1,6-Bisphosphatase Deficiency
branch: Cannot bypass PFK-1 step in reverse

disorder.name: Von Gierke Disease (GSD I)
branch: G6Pase absent → cannot release free glucose
G6P shunted → ↑ Lactate, ↑ Uric acid, ↑ Triglycerides

finalMolecule: Free Glucose → bloodstream

name: Glycogenesis
description: Synthesis of glycogen from glucose. Occurs in cytosol of liver (blood glucose maintenance) and skeletal muscle (local fuel reserve). Insulin promotes glycogenesis.

steps.cofactors: Initiates glycogen chain on Tyr residue
Active when dephosphorylated (insulin activates); forms α₁→4 linkages
Transfers 6–8 residues to form α₁→6 branch point

disorder.name: Andersen Disease (GSD IV)
branch: Branching enzyme absent → very few branches

finalMolecule: Branched Glycogen

name: Glycogenolysis
description: Degradation of glycogen to release glucose. Occurs in cytosol of liver (releases glucose to blood) and muscle (fuel for contraction). Activated by glucagon and epinephrine.

steps.cofactors: Pᵢ + PLP (Vit B6 prosthetic group); active when phosphorylated

disorder.name: McArdle Disease (GSD V) / Hers Disease (GSD VI)
branch: Muscle phosphorylase absent (McArdle) → no muscle glycogenolysis
Liver phosphorylase absent (Hers) → hepatomegaly, mild hypoglycaemia

steps.molecule: Limit Dextrin (4 residues from branch point)
steps.cofactors: Transfers trisaccharide + hydrolyses branch → free glucose

disorder.name: Cori Disease (GSD III)
branch: Glycogen broken down only to 'limit dextrin'

disorder.name: Von Gierke Disease (GSD I)
branch: G6Pase absent → G6P cannot be released as free glucose

finalMolecule: Free Glucose (liver) → bloodstream / G6P → Glycolysis (muscle)

name: Pyruvate Dehydrogenase (PDH) Complex
description: Irreversible oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate → Acetyl-CoA. Located in mitochondrial matrix. The essential link between glycolysis and the TCA cycle. Requires 5 coenzymes: TPP, NAD⁺, FAD, CoA, Lipoic acid.

disorder.name: Arsenite Poisoning
branch: Arsenite binds lipoic acid → blocks E2

steps.cofactors: FAD → FADH₂ → then NAD⁺ → NADH + H⁺

finalMolecule: Acetyl-CoA → TCA Cycle

name: TCA / Krebs / Citric Acid Cycle
description: Amphibolic cycle in mitochondrial matrix. Generates 10 ATP per turn: 3 NADH (7.5 ATP) + 1 FADH₂ (1.5 ATP) + 1 GTP (1 ATP). Provides precursors for heme, amino acids, and glucose.

steps.cofactors: H₂O; inhibited by ATP, NADH, Citrate
NAD⁺ → NADH + H⁺; CO₂ released; Mg²⁺; activated by ADP
NAD⁺+CoA+TPP+Lipoate+FAD → NADH; CO₂ released; inhibited by Arsenite

disorder.name: Arsenite / Arsenic Poisoning
branch: Arsenite binds lipoic acid on α-KG DH

finalMolecule: Oxaloacetate (regenerated → cycle repeats)

name: HMP Shunt (Pentose Phosphate Pathway)
description: Also: Dickens-Horecker Pathway. No ATP produced or consumed. Generates NADPH (for reductive biosynthesis and glutathione) and Ribose-5-P (for nucleotides). Active in liver, RBCs, adrenal cortex, mammary glands.

disorder.name: G6PD Deficiency
branch: Triggered by primaquine, dapsone, fava beans
X-linked recessive; most common enzyme deficiency worldwide

finalMolecule: Fructose-6-P + G3P (→ Glycolysis) + Ribose-5-P (→ Nucleotide synthesis)

name: Glucuronic Acid Pathway
description: Converts glucose → UDP-glucuronic acid (for bilirubin conjugation, detoxification, GAG synthesis). Also produces L-xylulose → HMP shunt. Humans cannot synthesise Vitamin C via this pathway (lack L-gulonolactone oxidase).

steps.cofactors: Required for Vitamin C synthesis; humans lack this enzyme

disorder.name: Scurvy (Vitamin C Deficiency)
branch: Deficiency → weak collagen → bleeding gums, loose teeth

disorder.name: Essential Pentosuria
branch: L-xylulose accumulates and excreted in urine
Gives false positive in old urine glucose tests (Benedict's)

finalMolecule: D-Xylulose-5-Phosphate → HMP Shunt

name: Polyol (Sorbitol) Pathway
description: Active in lens, seminal vesicles, Schwann cells, and retina. Converts glucose → sorbitol → fructose. Clinically significant in diabetes mellitus where glucose excess drives sorbitol accumulation.

disorder.name: Diabetic Cataract / Complications
branch: Excess glucose in lens → ↑ Sorbitol accumulation
Sorbitol is osmotically active and poorly diffusible
Also: Diabetic neuropathy (Schwann cells) and retinopathy
Aldose reductase inhibitors used to prevent this

steps.cofactors: NAD⁺ → NADH + H⁺; absent in lens

disorder.name: Sorbitol Accumulation in Lens
branch: Sorbitol cannot be converted to fructose

finalMolecule: Fructose (→ Fructose metabolism or used by sperm)

name: Fructose Metabolism
description: Liver pathway for fructose utilisation. Fructose bypasses PFK-1 (the rate-limiting step of glycolysis), so it is metabolised faster than glucose and promotes lipogenesis. Not insulin-dependent.

disorder.name: Hereditary Fructose Intolerance
branch: Liver damage, jaundice, vomiting after sucrose/fruit intake
Treatment: strict elimination of fructose and sucrose

finalMolecule: 2× Glyceraldehyde-3-Phosphate → Glycolysis

name: Galactose Metabolism
description: Converts galactose (from lactose digestion) to glucose-1-phosphate for entry into glycolysis. Occurs almost exclusively in the liver. Galactose not essential — can be synthesised from glucose via epimerase.

disorder.name: Galactokinase Deficiency
branch: Galactose reduced by aldose reductase to Galactitol
Galactitol accumulates in lens → osmotic cataract
Milder than classic galactosemia — no liver damage

disorder.name: Classical Galactosemia (Type I)
branch: E. coli sepsis risk in neonates
Treatment: strict lactose and galactose-free diet

finalMolecule: Glucose-1-Phosphate → Glycogenesis or Glycolysis

name: Cori Cycle (Lactic Acid Cycle)
description: Inter-organ cycle between skeletal muscle and liver. Muscle produces lactate anaerobically (2 ATP); liver converts it back to glucose (costs 6 ATP). Net deficit of 4 ATP = 'oxygen debt'. Provides continuous glucose supply during exercise.

steps.cofactors: Produces 2 ATP net under anaerobic conditions
NADH + H⁺ → NAD⁺ regenerated (essential for continued glycolysis)

disorder.name: Lactic Acidosis
branch: Excessive lactate production in hypoxia, shock
Muscle cramps from local lactate accumulation

steps.cofactors: NAD⁺ → NADH + H⁺; reverse reaction in well-oxygenated liver

finalMolecule: Glucose → released back to muscle

name: Glucose–Alanine (Cahill) Cycle
description: Inter-organ cycle between muscle and liver. Transfers amino nitrogen safely from muscle to liver as alanine (non-toxic). Liver detoxifies nitrogen as urea and converts pyruvate back to glucose. Critical during starvation.

disorder.name: Muscle Wasting in DM / Starvation
branch: Accelerated in uncontrolled diabetes and starvation
Muscle protein broken down for gluconeogenesis via this cycle
↑ ALT in blood = marker of liver damage (reverse reaction)

finalMolecule: Glucose → returned to muscle; NH₃ → Urea (liver)

name: BPG Shunt (Rapaport–Leubering Cycle)
description: Exclusive to erythrocytes. ~10% of glycolytic flux diverted here. Produces 2,3-BPG which decreases Hb-O₂ affinity (right-shifts ODC). No ATP generated — RBC sacrifices energy for O₂ delivery.

steps.cofactors: No energy input required; bypasses PGK step

disorder.name: PK Deficiency → ↑ 2,3-BPG
branch: In PK deficiency, glycolysis blocked at PEP step
↑ 2,3-BPG → right shift of ODC → O₂ delivered to tissues

steps.cofactors: H₂O; releases Pᵢ; re-enters glycolysis as 3-PG

disorder.name: Hexokinase Deficiency → ↓ 2,3-BPG
branch: ↓ 2,3-BPG → left shift of ODC → Hb holds O₂ tightly
O₂ not released to tissues effectively

finalMolecule: 3-Phosphoglycerate → re-enters Glycolysis at Step 8

name: β-Oxidation of Fatty Acids
description: Major energy-yielding pathway for fatty acids. Occurs in mitochondrial matrix. Sequentially removes 2-carbon units as Acetyl-CoA. Palmitate (16C): net 106 ATP. Requires carnitine shuttle for long-chain FA entry.

steps.cofactors: ATP → AMP + PPᵢ (= 2 high-energy bonds consumed); CoA-SH

disorder.name: Activation Step — 2 ATP equivalents consumed
branch: ATP is split to AMP (not ADP) — consumes 2 phosphate bonds
PPᵢ hydrolysed by pyrophosphatase → drives reaction forward
Carnitine deficiency prevents downstream transport (see Carnitine Shuttle)

steps.cofactors: Carnitine required; inhibited by Malonyl-CoA (fatty acid synthesis prevents breakdown simultaneously)

disorder.name: Carnitine Deficiency
branch: Seen in preterm infants (cannot synthesise carnitine)

steps.enzyme: Acyl-CoA Dehydrogenase (SCAD/MCAD/LCAD based on chain length)

finalMolecule: Acetyl-CoA (→ TCA Cycle) + FADH₂ + NADH (→ ETC) — cycle repeats with shortened chain

name: De Novo Fatty Acid Synthesis (Lynen's Spiral)
description: Synthesis of palmitate (16C) from Acetyl-CoA in cytosol. Requires 8 Acetyl-CoA + 14 NADPH + 7 ATP. Occurs in liver, adipose tissue, mammary glands. Stimulated by insulin, inhibited by glucagon.

steps.enzyme: Citrate Synthase (for export via Citrate Shuttle)
steps.cofactors: Condenses with OAA → Citrate for transport to cytosol
ATP + CO₂ + Biotin + Mn²⁺; inhibited by Palmitoyl-CoA; activated by Citrate

disorder.name: Malonyl-CoA Inhibits CAT-I (Cross-Pathway Regulation)
branch: Malonyl-CoA product inhibits CAT-I → prevents β-oxidation
Ensures FA synthesis and breakdown do not occur simultaneously
Statins → ↑ AMPK → inactivate ACC → ↓ FA synthesis

steps.cofactors: Ketoacyl synthase (CE); CO₂ released; chain attached to ACP

finalMolecule: Palmitate (16:0) → further elongation, desaturation, or esterification

name: Oxidation of Odd-Chain Fatty Acids
description: Odd-chain FA undergo β-oxidation normally until a 3-carbon Propionyl-CoA remains. Propionyl-CoA is then converted to Succinyl-CoA (TCA intermediate) via Vitamin B12-dependent steps. Odd-chain FA are gluconeogenic.

steps.cofactors: FAD, NAD⁺, CoA; produces Acetyl-CoA until 5C remains

disorder.name: Methylmalonic Acidemia
branch: Mutase deficient OR Vitamin B12 deficiency
Treatment: Vit B12 supplementation if B12-responsive form

finalMolecule: Succinyl-CoA → TCA Cycle (gluconeogenic — can form oxaloacetate → glucose)

name: Triacylglycerol Synthesis (Lipogenesis)
description: Synthesis of TAG from glycerol-3-phosphate and fatty acyl-CoA. Occurs in cytosol of liver and adipose tissue. Promoted by insulin (post-meal). Adipose tissue lacks glycerol kinase — must use DHAP from glycolysis.

steps.molecule: Glycerol-3-Phosphate (from DHAP in adipose; from glycerol in liver)

disorder.name: Adipose Tissue: No Glycerol Kinase
branch: Adipose tissue cannot phosphorylate free glycerol
Glycerol from lipolysis sent to liver for gluconeogenesis
Glycerol-3-P must be derived from DHAP (glycolysis)
Hence FA re-esterification in adipose requires active glycolysis (glucose)

disorder.name: Hypertriglyceridaemia / Fatty Liver
branch: Excess insulin → excess TAG synthesis in liver
Alcohol → excess NADH → excess FA esterification → fatty liver
LPL or Apo C-II deficiency → TAG not cleared → lipaemia
Eruptive xanthomas and pancreatitis risk at very high TAG levels

finalMolecule: Triacylglycerol (TAG) → stored in adipose or packaged into VLDL (liver)

name: Lipolysis (Fat Mobilisation)
description: Hydrolysis of stored TAG in adipose tissue to release Free Fatty Acids (FFA) and glycerol. Activated by glucagon, epinephrine, cortisol (via cAMP cascade). Inhibited by insulin. FFA → β-oxidation; glycerol → liver gluconeogenesis.

steps.enzyme: Hormone-Sensitive Lipase (HSL) — activated by phosphorylation via PKA
steps.cofactors: cAMP → PKA → phosphorylates HSL (active form); activated by glucagon/epinephrine

disorder.name: DKA — Uncontrolled Lipolysis
branch: In T1DM: no insulin → no HSL inhibition → uncontrolled lipolysis
FFA flood liver → converted to ketone bodies → DKA

finalMolecule: Glycerol (→ liver gluconeogenesis) + 3 Free Fatty Acids (→ β-oxidation)

name: Ketogenesis
description: Formation of ketone bodies (acetoacetate, β-hydroxybutyrate, acetone) exclusively in hepatic mitochondria. Occurs during starvation and in T1DM. Provides fuel for brain (up to 75% of energy) and other tissues when glucose is scarce.

steps.cofactors: + 1 more Acetyl-CoA; inhibited by Malonyl-CoA (level 2 regulation)

disorder.name: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)
branch: Kussmaul breathing (hyperventilation to blow off CO₂)

finalMolecule: Acetoacetate + β-Hydroxybutyrate (exported to tissues) + Acetone (exhaled)

name: Ketolysis (Ketone Body Utilisation)
description: Utilisation of ketone bodies in extrahepatic tissues (heart, renal cortex, skeletal muscle, brain). Liver cannot use ketones (lacks thiophorase). RBCs cannot (no mitochondria). Acetoacetate → 19 ATP; β-OHB → 21.5 ATP.

steps.cofactors: Succinyl-CoA → Succinate (donated); enzyme ABSENT in liver

disorder.name: Liver Cannot Utilise Ketones
branch: Liver lacks thiophorase — cannot activate acetoacetate
This ensures ketones flow out to peripheral tissues
If liver used its own ketones, the brain would be deprived
RBCs also cannot use ketones (no mitochondria)

finalMolecule: 2 Acetyl-CoA → TCA Cycle for complete oxidation

name: Cholesterol Biosynthesis (Mevalonate Pathway)
description: Synthesis of cholesterol from Acetyl-CoA. Occurs in cytosol and ER, primarily in liver. Requires 18 ATP + 14 NADPH per molecule. Rate-limiting enzyme: HMG-CoA reductase (statin target). Regulated by cellular cholesterol via SREBP.

steps.cofactors: 2 NADPH → 2 NADP⁺; inhibited by Statins, Glucagon, Cortisol; activated by Insulin, T4

disorder.name: Familial Hypercholesterolaemia
branch: LDL receptor defect (or Apo B-100 mutation)
Cannot clear LDL → ↑ plasma LDL → ↑ HMG-CoA reductase activity
Tendon xanthomas, corneal arcus, premature CAD
Statins competitively inhibit HMG-CoA reductase → ↓ endogenous cholesterol → ↑ LDL receptor expression

steps.cofactors: NADPH + O₂; forms steroid ring system

finalMolecule: Cholesterol (27C) → bile acids, steroid hormones, vitamin D, cell membranes

name: Bile Acid Synthesis
description: Conversion of cholesterol → primary bile acids (cholic acid, chenodeoxycholic acid) in liver ER. Only route for cholesterol excretion. Secondary bile acids formed by gut bacteria. Enterohepatic circulation recycles 95% of bile acids.

steps.cofactors: NADPH + Cytochrome P450 + Vit C; inhibited by bile acids (feedback)

disorder.name: Gallstone Disease (Cholelithiasis)
branch: Lithogenic bile: ↑ cholesterol relative to bile salts + lecithin
Bile salts keep cholesterol in solution (as micelles)
If bile salts ↓ → cholesterol precipitates → gallstones
Cholestyramine (bile acid resin) forces liver to convert more cholesterol → bile acids

steps.enzyme: Multiple hydroxylation and side-chain cleavage enzymes
steps.cofactors: Remove 3C as propionate; add hydroxyl groups

steps.molecule: Primary Bile Acids (Cholic acid + Chenodeoxycholic acid)

steps.cofactors: Forms secondary bile acids: Deoxycholic acid + Lithocholic acid

finalMolecule: Secondary Bile Acids → partially reabsorbed (enterohepatic circulation) → excreted in faeces

name: Lipoprotein Cascade (VLDL → IDL → LDL)
description: Endogenous lipid transport pathway. Liver secretes VLDL (TAG-rich). Lipoprotein lipase progressively strips TAG → IDL → LDL (cholesterol-rich). LDL ('bad cholesterol') taken up by LDL receptors or deposited in arterial walls.

disorder.name: Abetalipoproteinemia
branch: MTP gene mutation → cannot assemble VLDL/chylomicrons

steps.cofactors: Apo C-II activates LPL; Apo C-III inhibits; insulin induces LPL
Further TAG hydrolysis; cholesterol esters acquired from HDL via CETP

steps.enzyme: LDL Receptor (Apo B-100 receptor) — receptor-mediated endocytosis
steps.cofactors: Downregulated by high intracellular cholesterol (SREBP system)

disorder.name: Familial Hypercholesterolaemia
branch: Tuberous and tendon xanthomas, corneal arcus
Treatment: statins, bile acid resins, PCSK9 inhibitors

finalMolecule: Cholesterol delivered to peripheral tissues and liver

name: Reverse Cholesterol Transport
description: The ONLY pathway for cholesterol excretion from the body. HDL ('good cholesterol') collects excess cholesterol from peripheral tissues → delivers to liver → excreted as bile acids. PUFA required for LCAT activity.

steps.cofactors: Transfer free cholesterol to nascent discoid HDL

disorder.name: Tangier Disease
branch: Cholesterol cannot efflux from cells to HDL
Near-absent plasma HDL and Apo A-I

steps.cofactors: Apo A-I activates LCAT; PUFA required; esterifies free cholesterol → moves to core → HDL-3 (spherical)

disorder.name: LCAT Deficiency
branch: Cannot be excreted → accumulates in cornea, RBCs
Corneal clouding, anaemia, progressive renal failure

steps.cofactors: Exchanges CE from HDL for TAG from VLDL/LDL → forms HDL-2
Selective lipid uptake; Apo A-I recycled

finalMolecule: Cholesterol → liver → bile acids → excreted in faeces

name: HDL Cycle
description: Continuous interconversion between HDL-3 and HDL-2 in plasma. HDL-3 (smaller, denser) picks up cholesterol from tissues → LCAT esterifies it → HDL-2 (larger, CE-rich) → delivers to liver. Maintains effective reverse cholesterol transport.

steps.molecule: Discoid Nascent HDL (from liver and intestine)
steps.enzyme: ABC-A1 / ABC-G1 — cholesterol efflux from cells
steps.cofactors: Free cholesterol transferred to HDL surface
Lecithin donates fatty acid to cholesterol → Cholesterol Ester (CE); CE moves to HDL core → spherical HDL-3
Transfers CE from HDL to VLDL/LDL in exchange for TAG → HDL-2 formed; relieves LCAT product inhibition
Hydrolyses surface TAG and phospholipids → HDL-3 reformed (cycle continues)
Selective CE uptake; Apo A-I released back into circulation

finalMolecule: Cholesterol delivered to liver for bile synthesis; Apo A-I recycled to restart cycle

name: Carnitine Shuttle
description: Transports long-chain fatty acyl-CoA (LCFA-CoA) from cytosol into mitochondrial matrix for β-oxidation. Short and medium-chain FAs cross freely without carnitine. CAT-I is the rate-limiting, regulated step.

steps.cofactors: ATP → AMP + PPᵢ (2 high-energy bonds); CoA-SH

steps.enzyme: CAT-I (Carnitine Acyl Transferase I) — outer mitochondrial membrane

disorder.name: Carnitine Deficiency / CAT-I Deficiency
branch: LCFA accumulate in cytoplasm → lipid droplets in muscle/liver
Non-ketotic hypoglycaemia (cannot produce ketones from LCFA)
Carnitine synthesised from Lysine + Methionine (requires Vit C)

steps.cofactors: Antiport: Acyl-carnitine IN, free carnitine OUT

disorder.name: Translocase Deficiency
branch: Same clinical picture as carnitine deficiency

steps.enzyme: CAT-II (Carnitine Acyl Transferase II) — inner membrane, matrix side

finalMolecule: Long-Chain Acyl-CoA (in matrix) → β-Oxidation

name: Citrate Shuttle (Tricarboxylate Carrier System)
description: Transports Acetyl-CoA from mitochondrial matrix to cytosol for fatty acid synthesis. The inner mitochondrial membrane is impermeable to Acetyl-CoA directly. Citrate acts as the carrier molecule.

steps.cofactors: Citrate transported across inner mitochondrial membrane to cytosol

disorder.name: Citrate — Allosteric Regulator
branch: Citrate (in cytosol) allosterically activates Acetyl-CoA Carboxylase
Citrate also inhibits PFK-1 → slows glycolysis when energy sufficient
Links mitochondrial energy status to cytosolic FA synthesis

steps.cofactors: ATP + CoA → Acetyl-CoA + Oxaloacetate + ADP + Pᵢ

steps.enzyme: Malate Dehydrogenase → NADPH generation via Malic Enzyme
steps.cofactors: OAA → Malate (NADH); Malate → Pyruvate + NADPH (Malic Enzyme); Pyruvate re-enters mitochondria

finalMolecule: Acetyl-CoA (cytosol) → De Novo FA Synthesis

name: Vitamin K Cycle (Epoxide Cycle)
description: Vitamin K undergoes oxidation-reduction cycling in liver ER to continuously activate γ-glutamyl carboxylase. Required for post-translational γ-carboxylation of clotting factors II, VII, IX, X (and proteins C, S, Z). Target of warfarin.

steps.molecule: Vitamin K Hydroquinone (KH₂) — active reduced form
steps.cofactors: O₂; carboxylates Glu residues on clotting factors → γ-carboxyglutamate (GCG) allows Ca²⁺ binding

disorder.name: Vitamin K Deficiency / Haemorrhagic Disease
branch: Factors II, VII, IX, X cannot bind calcium → inactive
Haemorrhagic disease of the newborn (neonates lack gut flora)
Warfarin → anticoagulation by blocking this step

steps.cofactors: NADH; reduces Epoxide → Vitamin K Quinone

disorder.name: Warfarin / Dicoumarol — VKOR Inhibitors
branch: Vitamin K cannot be recycled → epoxide accumulates
Active hydroquinone depleted → clotting factors not carboxylated

steps.cofactors: NADH → completes the cycle; regenerates active Hydroquinone

finalMolecule: Vitamin K Hydroquinone (recycled for next γ-carboxylation reaction)

name: Proteolysis (Protein Digestion)
description: Hydrolytic degradation of dietary proteins to free amino acids. Carried out by hydrolases in stomach, pancreas, and small intestine. Enzymes secreted as inactive zymogens to prevent autodigestion.

disorder.name: Achlorhydria
branch: Associated with pernicious anaemia (also affects IF secretion)

steps.cofactors: Activated from pepsinogen by HCl; cleaves Phe, Tyr, Trp, Met bonds

disorder.name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
branch: Excess pepsin activity in ZE syndrome (gastrinoma)
PPI drugs inhibit H⁺/K⁺-ATPase → ↓ HCl → ↓ pepsin activation

steps.cofactors: Activated from trypsinogen by Enterokinase; cleaves Arg, Lys bonds; Trypsin also activates other zymogens

disorder.name: Acute Pancreatitis
branch: Premature activation of trypsinogen inside pancreas
Trypsin activates all other zymogens → autodigestion
Severe abdominal pain, raised serum amylase/lipase

steps.cofactors: All activated by trypsin; Carboxypeptidases require Zn²⁺
Act on N-terminal end; final release of free amino acids

finalMolecule: Free Amino Acids → portal blood → liver

name: Meister Cycle (γ-Glutamyl Cycle)
description: Active transport mechanism for neutral amino acids across cell membranes using glutathione as carrier. Costs 3 ATP per amino acid transported. Active in intestine, kidney tubules, and brain.

disorder.name: GGT — Clinical Marker of Alcohol Abuse
branch: Serum GGT rises proportionally with alcohol intake
Most sensitive marker for alcohol abuse
Also elevated in cholestatic liver disease and drug induction
GGT induction by alcohol: ↑ microsomal enzyme synthesis

steps.cofactors: Releases free amino acid into cell; forms 5-Oxoproline

finalMolecule: Glutathione (regenerated) → cycle restarts

name: Transamination
description: Reversible transfer of α-amino group from an amino acid to an α-keto acid. Operates via Ping-Pong (double displacement) mechanism. Occurs in virtually all tissues. No net deamination — amino group transferred, not released as NH₃.

steps.cofactors: Pyridoxal Phosphate (PLP / Vit B6) — forms Schiff base intermediate

disorder.name: Elevated ALT — Liver Damage Marker
branch: ALT highly specific for hepatocellular damage
↑ ALT in viral hepatitis, cirrhosis, NAFLD
De Ritis ratio: AST:ALT >2 suggests alcoholic hepatitis

steps.cofactors: PLP; key reaction: Oxaloacetate + Glutamate ⇌ Aspartate + α-KG

disorder.name: Elevated AST — Liver and Heart Damage
branch: AST present in liver, heart, skeletal muscle, RBCs
Rises in MI (now replaced by troponin)
Exceptions: Lysine, Threonine, Proline — do NOT undergo transamination

finalMolecule: Glutamate (collects amino groups) → Oxidative Deamination in liver mitochondria

name: Oxidative Deamination
description: Release of free ammonia (NH₃) from glutamate in hepatic mitochondria. The primary source of ammonia for the urea cycle. Glutamate is the only amino acid that undergoes rapid oxidative deamination in mammals.

steps.cofactors: NAD⁺ or NADP⁺; activated by ADP (low energy); inhibited by GTP (high energy)

disorder.name: Hyperammonaemia
branch: Failure to oxidatively deaminate glutamate → NH₃ accumulates
Liver failure → reduced GDH activity → NH₃ accumulation

finalMolecule: NH₃ → Urea Cycle | α-KG → TCA Cycle

name: Trans-deamination (Combined Pathway)
description: The physiologically dominant mechanism for amino nitrogen disposal. Combines transamination (all tissues, cytoplasm) and oxidative deamination (liver mitochondria). Glutamate acts as the central amino group collector.

steps.cofactors: PLP; transfers NH₂ to α-KG → forms Glutamate
Free glutamate or as glutamine; carried to hepatic portal circulation
NAD⁺ → NADH; releases free NH₃; regenerates α-KG

disorder.name: Ammonia Toxicity
branch: If GDH impaired (liver failure), glutamate accumulates
NH₃ not released → AA catabolism impaired
NH₃ inhibits α-KG dehydrogenase → TCA cycle blocked
α-KG depleted → brain energy failure → coma

finalMolecule: NH₃ → Urea Cycle | Carbon skeleton → TCA/Gluconeogenesis

name: Non-oxidative Deamination
description: Release of NH₃ from specific amino acids without oxidation. Provides an alternative deamination route for hydroxy and sulfur amino acids. Products feed into glycolysis and gluconeogenesis.

disorder.name: Histidinemia
branch: Histidase deficiency → ↑ blood and urine histidine
Speech defects and occasional mild mental retardation
Urocanic acid absent in skin (no UV protection)
Positive ferric chloride test in urine (grey-green)

finalMolecule: Pyruvate / α-Ketobutyrate + NH₃ → Urea Cycle

name: Urea Cycle (Krebs–Henseleit / Ornithine Cycle)
description: Converts toxic ammonia into non-toxic urea for excretion. Occurs exclusively in liver (mitochondria + cytosol). Costs 3 ATP (4 high-energy bonds) per urea molecule. Net cost ~1.5 after fumarate→NADH recovery. One N from NH₃, one from Aspartate.

steps.cofactors: 2 ATP; N-acetyl Glutamate (NAG) as obligate allosteric activator; Mg²⁺

disorder.name: Hyperammonaemia Type I (CPS-I Deficiency)
branch: CPS-I absent → NH₃ cannot enter urea cycle
No secondary orotic aciduria (distinguishes from OTC deficiency)

steps.cofactors: Forms Citrulline; Ornithine transported in via ORNT1

disorder.name: Hyperammonaemia Type II (OTC Deficiency)
branch: Excess carbamoyl-P enters pyrimidine pathway → ↑ Orotic acid in urine

steps.cofactors: ATP → AMP + PPᵢ (2 high-energy bonds); Mg²⁺
Cleaves to Arginine + Fumarate (fumarate enters TCA)

disorder.name: Hyperargininaemia (Arginase Deficiency)
branch: Symptoms appear later in childhood (unlike other UCDs)

finalMolecule: Urea → excreted in urine | Ornithine → recycled into mitochondria

name: One-Carbon Metabolism (Folate Cycle)
description: Pool of one-carbon units carried by Tetrahydrofolic acid (THFA). Supplies C2 and C8 for purine synthesis, methyl for dTMP synthesis, and methyl groups for transmethylation (via B12). Serine is the primary one-carbon donor. Methyl-THFA is a metabolic dead-end (irreversible).

steps.cofactors: PLP; transfers methylene group → Glycine + N⁵,N¹⁰-Methylene-THFA

disorder.name: Folate Trap (Vit B12 Deficiency)
branch: B12 needed to transfer methyl from N⁵-Methyl-THFA to Homocysteine
B12 deficient → methyl group cannot be transferred
Functional folate deficiency despite normal folate intake

steps.enzyme: Used by Purine Synthesis (C2 and C8 of purine ring)
steps.cofactors: Formyl group donated to growing purine ring

disorder.name: Folate Deficiency — FIGLU Test
branch: Histidine → FIGLU (Formiminoglutamate) in folic acid deficiency
FIGLU cannot transfer formimino group to THFA
↑ Urinary FIGLU after histidine load = diagnostic test for folate deficiency
Methotrexate blocks DHF→THFA → starves cells of one-carbon units

steps.cofactors: Methylene group transferred → dTMP; THFA oxidised to DHF

disorder.name: 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) Target
branch: 5-FU → FdUMP → suicide inhibitor of thymidylate synthase
dTMP synthesis blocked → no DNA synthesis
Methotrexate blocks DHF reductase → same net effect

finalMolecule: dTMP (DNA), Purines (DNA/RNA), Methionine (transmethylation)

name: Glycine–Serine–Choline Salvage Cycle
description: Salvages one-carbon units used in choline synthesis back into the folate pool. Serine → ethanolamine → choline (uses 3 SAM). Choline oxidised → betaine → donates methyls back via demethylation to regenerate glycine and one-carbon units.

steps.cofactors: Donates 1 methyl to Homocysteine → Methionine; becomes Dimethylglycine (B12-independent pathway)

disorder.name: Homocystinuria — Alternative Remethylation
branch: Betaine provides B12-independent route to remethylate Hcy
Reduces homocysteine levels even without B12
Dimethylglycine donates 2 more one-carbon units to THFA pool

steps.cofactors: NAD⁺; releases one-carbon units to THFA pool at each step

disorder.name: Nonketotic Hyperglycinaemia
branch: Massive ↑ glycine in blood, urine, and CSF
Severe neonatal seizures and mental retardation
Primary Hyperoxaluria: glyoxalate (glycine metabolite) → oxalate → kidney stones

finalMolecule: Glycine → THFA one-carbon pool replenished

name: Glycine Cleavage System
description: Major catabolic route for glycine. Multienzyme complex in mitochondria. Generates NADH, NH₃, CO₂, and a methylene one-carbon unit for THFA pool. Can run in reverse to synthesise glycine (glycine synthase mode).

steps.cofactors: Lipoamide prosthetic group; transfers methylamine to THFA

disorder.name: Nonketotic Hyperglycinaemia (NKH)
branch: Congenital defect in glycine cleavage system
↑↑ Glycine in blood, urine, and CSF
Seizures and severe mental retardation from birth
Treated partially with sodium benzoate (scavenges glycine)

finalMolecule: NH₃ + CO₂ + NADH + N⁵,N¹⁰-Methylene-THFA

name: Creatine–Creatinine Cycle
description: Synthesis of creatine from Arg + Gly + Met (via SAM). Phosphocreatine acts as immediate ATP buffer in muscle (Lohmann reaction). Creatinine is spontaneous non-enzymatic product excreted in urine at constant rate — used to estimate GFR.

steps.cofactors: Transfers amidino group from Arg to Gly; releases Ornithine
SAM (methyl donor) → SAH; methylation forms Creatine

disorder.name: Myocardial Infarction — CK-MB Marker
branch: CK-MB isoform specific to cardiac muscle
Troponin I more sensitive/specific now used

disorder.name: Renal Function Assessment
branch: Creatinine produced at constant rate (proportional to muscle mass)
Filtered at glomerulus, not reabsorbed → excreted in urine

finalMolecule: Creatinine → excreted in urine (GFR marker)

name: Trans-sulfuration Pathway (Methionine → Cysteine)
description: Converts essential amino acid methionine to non-essential cysteine via homocysteine. SAM (universal methyl donor) is generated as key intermediate. Requires PLP (B6) for both CBS and cystathionase steps.

steps.cofactors: ATP → PPᵢ + Pᵢ; forms SAM (active methionine / universal methyl donor)

disorder.name: SAM — Universal Methyl Donor
branch: SAM methylates: creatine, epinephrine, choline, melatonin, DNA
SAH is a potent product inhibitor of methyltransferases

steps.cofactors: SAM donates methyl group to acceptor molecules

disorder.name: Classical Homocystinuria (Type I)
branch: Treatment: B6 (if responsive), B12, folate, low-Met diet

steps.cofactors: PLP (Vit B6); cleaves to Cysteine + Homoserine

disorder.name: Cystathioninuria
branch: Homocysteine can be remethylated back to Methionine via B12/Folate

finalMolecule: Cysteine (non-essential AA) + Homoserine

name: Phenylalanine and Tyrosine Catabolism
description: Phenylalanine → Tyrosine → intermediates → Fumarate + Acetoacetate. Both glucogenic and ketogenic. Liver-based pathway. Multiple enzyme deficiencies give distinct disorders at each step.

steps.cofactors: Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) + NADPH + O₂; BH4 regenerated by DHPR

disorder.name: Phenylketonuria (PKU)
branch: Shunted to neurotoxic phenyl ketones (phenylacetate, phenyllactate)
Mental retardation, microcephaly, fair skin, mousy odour
Newborn Guthrie test screening (blood Phe >20 mg/dl)

disorder.name: Tyrosinaemia Type II (Richner-Hanhart)
branch: ↑↑ Tyrosine → crystallises in cornea and skin
Palmoplantar keratosis (hyperkeratosis of palms and soles)

steps.cofactors: Vit C (Ascorbate) + O₂; also hydroxylates ring → Homogentisate

disorder.name: Tyrosinaemia Type III
branch: Nitisinone (NTBC) inhibits this enzyme therapeutically in Type I

disorder.name: Alkaptonuria
branch: HGA accumulates → polymerises to black 'alkaptone' pigment
Ochronosis: black pigment deposits in cartilage, ear, sclerae
Severe debilitating arthritis in later life

disorder.name: Tyrosinaemia Type I (Hepatorenal)
branch: Succinylacetone formed → potent inhibitor of ALA dehydratase
Liver failure, renal tubular dysfunction (Fanconi syndrome)

finalMolecule: Fumarate (→ TCA/Gluconeogenesis) + Acetoacetate (→ Ketolysis)

name: BCAA Catabolism (Val, Leu, Ile)
description: Catabolism of branched-chain amino acids — Valine (glucogenic → Succinyl-CoA), Leucine (ketogenic → Acetyl-CoA + Acetoacetate), Isoleucine (both → Acetyl-CoA + Propionyl-CoA). Mainly in skeletal muscle, heart, brain (minimal in liver). Entirely mitochondrial.

steps.enzyme: Branched-Chain α-Keto Acid Dehydrogenase (BCKD) Complex — Rate-Limiting
steps.cofactors: TPP + Lipoate + FAD + NAD⁺ + CoA (same cofactors as PDH); oxidative decarboxylation → Acyl-CoA derivatives

disorder.name: Maple Syrup Urine Disease (MSUD)
branch: BCKD complex deficient → BCAA and keto acids accumulate
Burnt sugar / maple syrup odour of urine
Severe neonatal encephalopathy, seizures, mental retardation
Treatment: BCAA-restricted diet; high-dose Thiamine (if responsive)

disorder.name: Isovaleric Acidaemia
branch: Isovaleric acid: characteristic 'sweaty feet' cheesy odour
Positive DNPH test; elevated C5 acylcarnitine on MS/MS

steps.cofactors: Val → Succinyl-CoA (via Propionyl-CoA + B12); Leu → Acetoacetate + Acetyl-CoA; Ile → Propionyl-CoA + Acetyl-CoA

finalMolecule: Succinyl-CoA (Val) + Acetyl-CoA/Acetoacetate (Leu) + Acetyl-CoA/Propionyl-CoA (Ile)

name: Kynurenine Pathway (Tryptophan → Niacin)
description: Tryptophan catabolism via kynurenine pathway generates NAD⁺/Niacin. 60 mg dietary tryptophan → 1 mg Niacin. Vitamin B6 (PLP) is essential cofactor. Blockade leads to functional niacin deficiency and pellagra.

steps.cofactors: Heme (Fe²⁺) + O₂; induced by cortisol and tryptophan

disorder.name: Carcinoid Syndrome
branch: Carcinoid tumour diverts up to 60% tryptophan → Serotonin synthesis
Kynurenine pathway starved of substrate → Niacin deficiency

disorder.name: Vit B6 Deficiency / INH-Induced Pellagra
branch: Kynureninase requires PLP → B6 deficiency blocks this step
↑ Urinary xanthurenic acid = diagnostic test for B6 deficiency
Isoniazid (INH) is B6 antagonist → induces B6 deficiency → pellagra
Hartnup disease: Trp not absorbed → pellagra-like rash

steps.cofactors: PRPP; Quinolinate → Nicotinic acid mononucleotide → NAD⁺

finalMolecule: NAD⁺ / NADP⁺ (Niacin-containing coenzymes) + Alanine

name: GABA Shunt
description: Alternative route from Glutamate → Succinate in the brain, bypassing α-KG dehydrogenase step of TCA. GABA is the major inhibitory neurotransmitter in CNS. PLP essential for both enzymatic steps. Step 1 cytoplasmic, steps 2–3 mitochondrial.

disorder.name: Infantile Convulsions (B6 Deficiency)
branch: B6 deficiency → ↓ GABA synthesis → loss of CNS inhibition
Pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy: genetic variant needs pharmacological B6 doses

disorder.name: Valproate — GABA-T Inhibitor
branch: Sodium valproate inhibits GABA transaminase (GABA oxidase)
↑ GABA levels in synaptic cleft → enhanced inhibition
Used in epilepsy, bipolar disorder, migraine prophylaxis
GABA-T also inhibited by Vigabatrin (γ-vinyl GABA) — irreversible

disorder.name: Succinic Semialdehyde Dehydrogenase Deficiency
branch: ↑ γ-Hydroxybutyric acid (GHB) in urine, CSF, plasma
Hydroxybutyric aciduria on urine organic acids

finalMolecule: Succinate → TCA Cycle

name: Catecholamine Synthesis
description: Tyrosine → DOPA → Dopamine → Norepinephrine → Epinephrine. Occurs in adrenal medulla, sympathetic ganglia, and brain. Rate-limiting step: Tyrosine Hydroxylase (TH). SAM donates methyl for final step.

steps.cofactors: BH4 + NADPH + O₂; BH4 regenerated by DHPR; inhibited by catecholamines (feedback)

disorder.name: Parkinson's Disease (Dopamine Deficiency)
branch: Loss of dopaminergic neurons in substantia nigra
↓ Dopamine → loss of inhibition of motor pathway → rigidity, tremor

steps.cofactors: Vit C (Ascorbate) + Cu²⁺ + O₂; hydroxylation → Norepinephrine (stored in chromaffin granules)

disorder.name: Pheochromocytoma
branch: Episodic hypertension, palpitations, headache, sweating ('5 Ps')
VMA formed by MAO + COMT degradation

steps.cofactors: SAM (methyl donor); SAH released; only in adrenal medulla (induced by cortisol from adrenal cortex)

finalMolecule: Epinephrine (Adrenaline) → secreted into blood

name: Serotonin and Melatonin Synthesis
description: Tryptophan → Serotonin (5-HT) in brain, platelets, GIT. Serotonin → Melatonin in pineal gland (darkness-induced). PLP essential for decarboxylation. SAM for methylation step. Serotonin catabolised to 5-HIAA.

disorder.name: Carcinoid Syndrome / Depression
branch: Carcinoid: ↑↑ serotonin synthesis → flushing, diarrhoea, wheezing
Depression: ↓ serotonin → SSRIs inhibit reuptake → ↑ synaptic 5-HT

steps.cofactors: Acetyl-CoA; rhythm driven by darkness/melatonin pathway

disorder.name: Circadian Rhythm Disorders
branch: Melatonin regulates sleep-wake cycle and circadian rhythms
Pineal gland secretion controlled by light/dark cycles (SCN)
Exogenous melatonin used for jet lag, insomnia
Serotonin catabolism: MAO → 5-HIAA → excreted in urine

finalMolecule: Melatonin (pineal) + Serotonin (brain/gut/platelets)

name: Melanin Synthesis
description: Tyrosine → DOPA → DOPAquinone → Melanin in melanosomes of melanocytes. Tyrosinase (Cu²⁺-dependent) catalyses first two steps. Eumelanin (black/brown) vs Pheomelanin (red/yellow) depending on cysteine availability.

disorder.name: Albinism
branch: Tyrosinase absent → no DOPA → no melanin
Total lack of pigment in skin, hair, iris (oculocutaneous albinism)
Photophobia, nystagmus, high skin cancer risk
Menke's disease: Cu²⁺ transport defect → secondary tyrosinase failure

disorder.name: Vitiligo (Leucoderma)
branch: Autoimmune destruction of melanocytes in patches
Loss of pigment in localised skin areas
Associated with thyroid disease, T1DM, pernicious anaemia
MSH (Melanocyte Stimulating Hormone) normally stimulates melanin dispersal

finalMolecule: Eumelanin (black/brown) or Pheomelanin (red/yellow) → UV protection

name: Ubiquitin–Proteasome Pathway
description: ATP-dependent degradation of short-lived, misfolded, or abnormal proteins. Ubiquitin tags mark proteins for 26S proteasome digestion. Discovered by Ciechanover, Hershko & Rose (Nobel 2004). PEST sequences target rapid degradation.

steps.cofactors: ATP; forms high-energy thioester bond with ubiquitin
Transfers ubiquitin from E1 to E2
Attaches ubiquitin to Lys residue on target; polyubiquitination (4+ chains required)

disorder.name: Angelman Syndrome / Von Hippel-Lindau
branch: VHL E3 ligase defect → HIF-α not degraded → ↑ VEGF → angiomas
Cachexia in cancer/AIDS: inflammatory cytokines activate ubiquitin pathway → muscle wasting

steps.cofactors: ATP for unfolding; proteases in 20S barrel digest protein → oligopeptides

disorder.name: Parkinson's / Alzheimer's — Proteasome Overload
branch: Misfolded α-synuclein overwhelms proteasome in Parkinson's
Alzheimer's: amyloid-β and tau resist degradation
Bortezomib: proteasome inhibitor used in multiple myeloma treatment

finalMolecule: Oligopeptides (5–6 AA) → further hydrolysis to free amino acids

name: Heme Biosynthesis (Porphyrin Synthesis)
description: Synthesis of heme from Succinyl-CoA + Glycine. Occurs in bone marrow (80%) and liver (20%). First and last 3 steps in mitochondria; middle steps in cytosol. Rate-limiting enzyme: ALA Synthase (requires PLP). Lead and INH inhibit key steps.

steps.cofactors: PLP (Vit B6); Mg²⁺; produces ALA + CO₂; inhibited by heme (feedback) and glucose (high glucose suppresses)

disorder.name: Sideroblastic Anaemia (INH-induced)
branch: Isoniazid (INH) is Vit B6 antagonist → PLP unavailable
ALA synthase impaired → haem synthesis fails
Iron accumulates in mitochondria → ring sideroblasts on marrow biopsy
Sideroblastic anaemia; responds to Pyridoxine (B6) supplementation

steps.cofactors: 2 ALA → PBG; Zn²⁺ required; inhibited by Lead

disorder.name: Lead Poisoning / Plumbism
branch: Lead binds SH-groups → inhibits ALA dehydratase AND ferrochelatase
↑ ALA in urine (neurotoxic) → peripheral neuropathy, wrist drop
Burton's line (blue lead deposits on gums)

steps.cofactors: 4 PBG → linear HMB tetrapyrrole; then UPG-III Cosynthase → UPG-III

disorder.name: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP)
branch: Acute abdominal pain, neuropathy, psychosis — NO photosensitivity
Urine turns red/purple on standing (PBG → porphyrins)
Avoid: barbiturates, alcohol, OCP, sulfonamides → all induce ALA synthase → worsen AIP
Treatment: haematin infusion + high glucose (suppress ALA synthase)

steps.cofactors: Decarboxylation of 4 acetate side chains → CPG-III

disorder.name: Porphyria Cutanea Tarda (PCT)
branch: Blisters, scarring, hypertrichosis on light-exposed skin
Associated with alcohol, hepatitis C, iron overload

disorder.name: Hereditary Coproporphyria (HCP)
branch: Both acute attacks (like AIP) AND photosensitivity
Coproporphyrins excreted in urine and faeces

steps.cofactors: Fe²⁺ (ferrous iron); inhibited by Lead; requires Fe²⁺ not Fe³⁺

disorder.name: Erythropoietic Protoporphyria (EPP)
branch: Ferrochelatase deficiency → protoporphyrin accumulates in RBCs
Severe photosensitivity; RBC fluorescence under UV

finalMolecule: Heme (Fe²⁺-Protoporphyrin IX) → Hb, myoglobin, cytochromes, catalase

name: Heme Catabolism (Heme → Bilirubin)
description: Degradation of heme from senescent RBCs (120-day lifespan) in reticuloendothelial cells of liver, spleen, bone marrow. Only reaction in human body producing CO as byproduct. Generates 250–300 mg bilirubin daily.

steps.cofactors: Globin → amino acids (recycled); heme ring liberated
NADPH + O₂; alpha-methenyl bridge cleaved; CO released (only endogenous CO source); Fe²⁺ released → recycled

disorder.name: Haemolytic Jaundice (Pre-hepatic)
branch: Causes: G6PD deficiency, sickle cell, thalassaemia, ABO incompatibility

disorder.name: Shunt Bilirubin (15% of total)
branch: Heme/Hb precursors degraded before leaving marrow (ineffective erythropoiesis)
Identified by rapid excretion of radiolabelled glycine (within 10 days)

finalMolecule: Unconjugated Bilirubin (lipophilic) → bound to albumin → transported to liver

name: Bilirubin Transport, Conjugation and Excretion
description: Unconjugated bilirubin (UCB) transported on albumin to liver → uptaken by hepatocytes → conjugated with glucuronic acid → secreted into bile → bacterial reduction in gut → urobilinogen → excreted in stool/urine.

disorder.name: Kernicterus / Drug Displacement
branch: Deposits in basal ganglia → kernicterus (brain damage in neonates)
Normal: UCB >20 mg/dl saturates albumin → free UCB rises
Aspirin, sulfonamides, penicillin → displace bilirubin from albumin
Phototherapy: isomerises UCB to water-soluble isomers for excretion

steps.cofactors: Carrier-mediated; intracellular binding to Ligandin (Y protein) and Z protein
UDP-Glucuronic acid (from glucuronic acid pathway); forms BMG then BDG (bilirubin diglucuronide = direct bilirubin)

disorder.name: Gilbert's Syndrome / Crigler-Najjar Syndrome
branch: Gilbert's: UGT1A1 promoter mutation (TA repeat) → mild UCB elevation (<4 mg/dl); benign, common (5% population)
Gilbert's: jaundice triggered by fasting, stress, illness; normal liver enzymes; normal urine bilirubin
Crigler-Najjar Type I: Complete UGT absence → extreme UCB (20–45 mg/dl) → kernicterus → death in infancy
Crigler-Najjar Type II: Partial UGT → UCB <20 mg/dl; responds to Phenobarbitone (induces UGT)
Neonatal jaundice: transient low UGT → physiological jaundice (d1–d7)
Phenobarbitone induces UGT → used to treat Gilbert's and Crigler-Najjar Type II

steps.cofactors: Active transport against concentration gradient into bile canaliculi — rate-limiting step of heme catabolism

disorder.name: Dubin-Johnson Syndrome / Rotor Syndrome
branch: Dubin-Johnson: MRP-2 mutation → conjugated bilirubin regurgitates into blood
BSP test: secondary peak at 90 min
Rotor: OATP 1B1/1B3 mutation → hepatic re-uptake of conjugated BR fails

steps.cofactors: Deconjugation → free bilirubin → reduced to Urobilinogen (UBG) and Stercobilinogen (SBG)

disorder.name: Obstructive (Post-hepatic) Jaundice
branch: BDG cannot reach intestine → no UBG formed
Bilirubinuria (direct bilirubin filtered by kidney → dark urine)
Acholic stools + dark urine = obstructive jaundice

finalMolecule: Stercobilin (brown stool colour) + Urobilin (yellow urine colour) — 20% UBG reabsorbed (enterohepatic circulation)

name: De Novo Purine Synthesis
description: Synthesis of purine ring directly on ribose-5-phosphate. Costs 6 ATP per nucleotide. Occurs in liver cytoplasm. Purine ring atoms: N1 (Asp), C2 (Formate via THFA), N3 (Gln), C4,C5,N7 (Gly), C6 (CO₂), N9 (Gln), C8 (Formate). IMP is the first purine nucleotide formed.

steps.cofactors: ATP → AMP + Pᵢ; forms PRPP (Phosphoribosyl Pyrophosphate)

disorder.name: Primary Gout (PRPP Synthetase Overactivity)
branch: PRPP synthetase overactivity OR loss of feedback inhibition
↑ PRPP → ↑ de novo purine synthesis → ↑ uric acid
Hyperuricaemia → monosodium urate crystals in joints
Podagra: acute arthritis of big toe

steps.cofactors: Glutamine + H₂O; releases PPᵢ; forms 5-phosphoribosylamine; inhibited by AMP, GMP, IMP (feedback)
Gly, Formate (N10-formyl-THFA), Gln, CO₂, Asp; multiple ATP consumed

steps.enzyme: Adenylosuccinate Synthetase (for AMP) / IMP Dehydrogenase (for GMP)
steps.cofactors: GTP for AMP branch; NAD⁺ + ATP for GMP branch; cross-regulation (AMP synthesis needs GTP; GMP synthesis needs ATP)

finalMolecule: AMP / GMP → ADP/GDP → ATP/GTP

name: Purine Salvage Pathway
description: Recycling of preformed purine bases to nucleotides. Economises energy vs de novo synthesis. Essential in RBCs and brain (minimal de novo capacity). HGPRTase salvages hypoxanthine and guanine; APRTase salvages adenine. PRPP is mandatory ribose donor.

disorder.name: APRTase Deficiency
branch: Diagnosed by orange-red crystals in urine

disorder.name: Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome
branch: Hypoxanthine and Guanine not salvaged → degraded → ↑↑ Uric acid (9–11 mg/dl)
PRPP accumulates → drives ↑ de novo purine synthesis

finalMolecule: IMP / AMP / GMP → re-enter nucleotide pool

name: Purine Nucleotide Degradation (Uric Acid Formation)
description: Catabolism of AMP and GMP → Uric acid. Humans lack uricase (found in other mammals) → cannot convert uric acid to soluble allantoin. Uric acid has low solubility (6.8 mg/dl at pH 7.4) → precipitates as monosodium urate crystals.

disorder.name: PNP Deficiency
branch: PNP absent → inosine and guanosine accumulate → dGTP accumulates
Inhibits ribonucleotide reductase → T cell deficiency (primarily)
Combined immunodeficiency but B cells relatively spared

steps.cofactors: FAD + Mo + Fe²⁺ + O₂; produces H₂O₂ as byproduct

disorder.name: Gout / Xanthinuria
branch: Gout: ↑ Uric acid (>7 mg/dl) → MSU crystal deposition in joints
Podagra (1st MTP joint), tophi, urate nephropathy
Allopurinol → competitive substrate → mechanism-based inhibition of XO → ↑ Hypoxanthine/Xanthine (more soluble)
Xanthinuria: XO deficiency → ↓ Uric acid → xanthine stones
Rasburicase: recombinant uricase (tumour lysis syndrome treatment)

finalMolecule: Uric Acid → excreted in urine (350–600 mg/day)

name: De Novo Pyrimidine Synthesis
description: Pyrimidine ring synthesised FIRST, then attached to PRPP (opposite to purine synthesis). First 3 enzymes form CAD trifunctional complex. Step 4 in mitochondria (unique). Rate-limiting: CPS-II (cytoplasmic; uses glutamine). CPS-I (mitochondrial) is for Urea Cycle.

steps.cofactors: 2 ATP; glutamine (not free NH₃); inhibited by UTP; activated by PRPP

disorder.name: Secondary Orotic Aciduria (OTC Deficiency)
branch: OTC deficiency → excess Carbamoyl-P leaks from mitochondria to cytosol
Enters pyrimidine pathway → floods CPS-II step
↑↑ Orotic acid synthesised → excreted in urine
Key distinguishing feature of OTC deficiency from CPS-I deficiency
No orotic aciduria in CPS-I deficiency

steps.cofactors: NAD⁺ → NADH; only mitochondrial step; inhibited by Leflunomide

disorder.name: Leflunomide (DHODH Inhibitor)
branch: Leflunomide inhibits DHODH → ↓ UMP synthesis → ↓ lymphocyte proliferation
Used as immunosuppressant in rheumatoid arthritis
Teriflunomide (active metabolite) used in multiple sclerosis

disorder.name: Hereditary Orotic Aciduria
branch: Cannot convert orotic acid to UMP
Treatment: Uridine supplementation (bypasses block + restores UTP feedback)

steps.cofactors: CO₂ released; forms UMP — first pyrimidine nucleotide

finalMolecule: UMP / CTP → dUMP → dTMP (via Thymidylate Synthase)

name: Pyrimidine Degradation
description: Pyrimidines degraded to highly water-soluble products (β-alanine and β-amino isobutyrate) — unlike purines (insoluble uric acid). No clinical stone formation. β-alanine used for carnosine and CoA synthesis.

disorder.name: DPD Deficiency — 5-FU Toxicity / Pseudouridinuria
branch: DPD deficiency → 5-FU not degraded → severe drug toxicity
Mucositis, myelosuppression, neurotoxicity after standard 5-FU dose
DPYD gene testing recommended before 5-FU chemotherapy
Pseudouridine (from tRNA) not further degraded → excreted unchanged in urine (marker of DPD deficiency)
No clinical consequences — detected on urine metabolomics

finalMolecule: β-Alanine (→ Carnosine / CoA) + β-Amino Isobutyrate (→ excreted in urine)

name: Deoxyribonucleotide Synthesis (Ribonucleotide Reductase)
description: Reduction of ribonucleoside diphosphates (NDPs) → deoxyribonucleoside diphosphates (dNDPs) for DNA synthesis. Rate-limiting step for DNA replication. Requires NADPH via Thioredoxin system. Balances dNTP pools.

steps.cofactors: NADPH → Thioredoxin (reduced) → RNR; non-heme Fe; reduces 2'-OH to 2'-H

disorder.name: ADA Deficiency (SCID)
branch: dATP is potent general inhibitor of RNR
All dNTP pools depleted → DNA replication blocked
Lymphocytes cannot proliferate (rapidly dividing cells most affected)
SCID: absent T and B cells → fatal infections in infancy without treatment

steps.cofactors: ATP → phosphorylation → dNTPs (dATP, dGTP, dCTP, dUTP)
Rapidly converts dUTP → dUMP + PPᵢ (prevents dU incorporation into DNA)
N5,N10-Methylene-THFA → methyl donor; DHF produced (must be regenerated by DHFR)

disorder.name: Methotrexate / 5-FU — Cancer Targets
branch: Methotrexate: DHF reductase inhibitor → THFA not regenerated → thymidylate synthase starved
5-FU → FdUMP: suicide inhibitor of thymidylate synthase
Both drugs → ↓ dTMP → DNA synthesis failure
Leucovorin (folinic acid) used as rescue to replenish THFA

finalMolecule: dTMP / dATP / dGTP / dCTP → DNA synthesis
